title: Check your understanding: Programmatic Access to Git

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of programmatic access to git?
options: Programmatic Git access can call the Git executable or use a language library. The executable is often the most portable baseline, but scripts must pass arguments safely and handle errors, paths and platform differences.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: Programmatic Git access can call the Git executable or use a language library. The executable is often the most portable baseline, but scripts must pass arguments safely and handle errors, paths and platform differences.
questions.explanation: Programmatic Git access can call the Git executable or use a language library. The executable is often the most portable baseline, but scripts must pass arguments safely and handle errors, paths and platform differences.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git -C path/to/repository status --short --branch` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with programmatic access to git?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
